notes: Read the complete unit, Social Security and Medicare context, all nine candidates and the review. Limited earned-benefit protection to the three governing programs, resolved the self-employed contribution as 12.4 percent, named Social Security as the program to strengthen, preserved look to expand as exploratory rather than a firm commitment, and restored lifetime paycheck contributions and the importance of dental, vision and hearing services.

claims.claim_text: Generations of Americans have paid into Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid from every paycheck throughout their working lives.
Democrats reject cutting benefits Americans have earned under Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid.
Self-employed Americans pay 12.4 percent of income to support Social Security, twice the stated middle-class rate.
Democrats would strengthen Social Security and expand its benefits by asking the wealthiest Americans to pay what the party considers their fair share.
Democrats would look to expand traditional Medicare to dental, vision and hearing services, which they characterize as important to health and quality of life.
That possible Medicare expansion would be financed by making wealthy people and large corporations pay what Democrats consider their fair share.
